title: Burndown to SLA coverage mapping and discount heuristics
content:
Purpose:
This working sheet maps projected cash burndown (net burn) to the minimal SLA coverage we must maintain (GPU-hours / burst-reserve) and proposes a set of discount heuristics tied to soft-commit thresholds. Intended audience: finance, FP&A, commercial ops, and SRE leads for capacity planning alignment.

High-level summary (TL;DR):
- If net run-rate burn reduces available runway below 22 weeks, trigger hiring freeze + pause of non-essential Dedicated capacity expansion.
- Maintain 95th-percentile SLA coverage for enterprise customers; for freemium/PLG tiers, allow targeted coverage degradation scaled to discount bands.
- Discounts should be gated by committed token / capacity floors and a decommit notice window; avoidance of ad-hoc discounts is primary objective.

Assumptions (editable):
- Baseline monthly gross burn: $5.2M (run-rate Aug 2026).
- Average price per 1k tokens (hosted mix): $0.35 effective after current promotions.
- GPU mix: 60% A100 80GB, 30% H100, 10% spare spot instances for burst.
- Typical token velocity per active customer: 45k tokens/day (median).

Scenario table (compact view):
Columns: Scenario | Monthly burn | Runway (wks) | SLA coverage target | Headcount delta | Discount band
- Base | $5.2M | 38 | 95% enterprise / 80% PLG | +0 | 0%
- Contraction | $6.0M | 32 | 95% enterprise / 70% PLG | -4 FTE | 5-10% on >12mo commit
- Burst-demand | $6.8M | 28 | 98% enterprise / 90% PLG | +6 FTE (short term) | 0-5% with strict capacity SLAs
- Cost-optimization | $4.1M | 51 | 92% enterprise / 65% PLG | -8 FTE + quantization rollout | 10-20% for 24mo commit + capacity limits

Headcount phasing (quarterly snapshot):
- Q4 2026 (plan): hiring pause for non-revenue eng; prioritize SRE + infra (2 hires deferred -> moved to Q2 2027).
- Q1 2027: conditional re-open if burn < $4.8M/mo or ARR growth > 12%/qtr.
- Hot roles: SRE (2), Serving-runtime engineer (1), Commercial ops analyst (1).

Discount heuristics (proposal):
- Band A: 0% discount. Requirements: month-to-month or <6mo commit, no capacity reservation.
- Band B: 5% discount. Requirements: >=12mo commit, maximum sustained token floor and 30d decommit.
- Band C: 10-15% discount. Requirements: >=24mo commit, defined capacity slab, prepay / committed spend, explicit SLA coverage tradeoff agreed in contract.
- Auto-expiry: All discounts re-evaluated every 6 months with usage reconciliation.

SLA coverage mapping rules (how we map burn -> capacity):
1) Compute minimal reserved pool required to keep 95% P99 latency under expected peak load = baseline 1.25x median GPU-hours.
2) For each $100k of incremental monthly burn reduction we accept decreasing reserved pool by ~1.6% (empirical from internal sim).
3) If runway < 30 weeks, freeze expansion of reserved pools and push new customers to burst-only routing until commit or pricing adjustments.

Sample micro-slab pricing table (for simulation sheet):
Slab name | Monthly commitment ($) | Effective discount | Capacity cap (GPU-hours/day)
Core-12 | 50,000 | 0% | 80
Core-50 | 200,000 | 5% | 330
Core-200 | 800,000 | 12% | 1,400
Enterprise-flex | 1,500,000+ | 18%+ | negotiated with coverage floor

Financial triggers and playbook (operational):
- Trigger A (alert): runway < 32 weeks -> Finance ops prepares hiring freeze memo, product rate-limit options, and a pricing standing committee review.
- Trigger B (action): runway < 26 weeks or sequential month-over-month revenue decline -> immediate 6-week hiring pause and re-evaluate discounts on a cohort basis.
- Trigger C (escalate): runway < 20 weeks -> leadership review for emergency measures (one-time credits, repricing, L2 compensation adjustments).

Open questions / risks (work-in-progress):
- How to quantify customer churn from stricter discount gating? Need historic cohort analysis (action: Priya to pull cohort churn vs discount acceptance).
- Correlation between quantization adoption and unit-cost reduction is model dependent; we currently assume 9-12% savings on token cost for warm models. Validate with serving-runtime team.
- Legal contract lead time for 24mo commitments often exceeds 6 weeks — operational mismatch with our 30d decommit window.

Next steps / action items:
- [Aisha] Build simulation tab that models burndown -> capacity scaling at 1% granularity (due 2026-11-08).
- [Luca] Pull cohort churn vs discount acceptance (due 2026-11-05).
- [Ryan] Run quick kernel-level cost check for quantization savings on H100 (due 2026-11-12).
- Schedule cross-functional review with SRE and Commercial Ops the week of 2026-11-15.

Notes to reviewers: this sheet is intentionally lightweight and conservative on discount exposure. Feedback wanted on the mapping coefficient (1.6% per $100k) — empirical inputs welcome.

Revision history (brief):
- 2026-09-21 created initial draft and scenario skeleton.
- 2026-10-12 inserted micro-slab table and early discount bands.
- 2026-11-01 updated headcount phasing and added triggers per leadership ask.
notes: informal working sheet — contains assumptions and provisional heuristics; not final policy
